10. Decisive smaller experiment

The next physical test should exercise a full-size pod, both escape boundaries and the actual cutter—not merely a release coupon.

The proposed budget is $62,537, including contingency.

Physical test construction

Use:

One full-size opposed-pad pod and normal foot.
Actual neck/root cartridges.
Original and replacement joint coupons.
False-seat and partial-engagement inserts.
Pod-owned cage.
Openable reciprocating saw cassette.
Independently removable blade-end cartridge.
A positive primary catch fixture.
A guarded 3 J energy-injection fixture.
A 30 kN test-machine access route.

Commercial universal testing machines are available in the required force range; the quoted access costs here are allowances, not bookings. 
ZwickRoell

Itemized budget
Group	Included work	Cost
Pod, necks and joint specimens	Full pod, member/foot necks, false-seat parts	$7,920
Primary catch, cage and energy fixture	Positive replacement path, capture and guarded injection	$4,400
Cutter and drive	Feed, crank, measurement, openable cassette	$4,500
Base, sensors, controller and fault hardware	Reaction fixtures, independent strain channels, perturbation jig, isolation	$7,950
Instrument access	Test machine, reference cell, DAQ, displacement, imaging and inspection	$12,250
Engineering, execution and reset	Drawings, assembly, calibration, blind challenges, analysis and final restoration	$17,360
Contingency	15%	$8,157
Total		$62,537
Matched protocol

Conduct 80 attempts:

Forty candidate attempts.
Forty competent assisted-control attempts.
Twenty-eight nominal and twelve blind challenge attempts per route.

Both routes receive the same load, access, interfaces, observations, independent escape and inspection criteria. Challenge identity is withheld from the controller/operator until the attempt ends.

Use several load levels and both signs. Include persistent and partly open jams, false engagement, seized final receiver, friction/bias variation and one-hour outages.

Measure independently:

Applied load.
Both pad reactions.
Replacement reaction and transient peaks.
Cage and foot reactions.
Relative displacement during every transfer.
Screw, lock and retention states.
Blade speed, force, feed, tension and runout.
Full wall energy.
All fragments, rejected hardware and returned stocks.
Wear, permanent set and before/after sensor bias.

The discriminating result
